sections.heading: B — Audience and scope
sections.markdown:
## B — Audience and scope

Audience: first-time Hawaii class three applicants, including minors on the graduated path, learning the scale of the drinking-driver problem, how alcohol acts on the body, the implied consent and administrative revocation laws, zero tolerance for drivers under twenty-one, impairment thresholds, open container rules and the effects of prescription, over-the-counter and illegal drugs in plain English.

Prerequisites: the licensing bars from the first section, where a drunk driving conviction while unlicensed already appeared as a two-year bar.

Scope note: the scale of alcohol-involved fatal crashes, how alcohol acts and what does not sober a drinker, the prohibition on driving under the influence, implied consent, administrative revocation and the thirty-day permit, refusal penalties, the impaired and under-the-influence thresholds, zero tolerance for drivers under twenty-one, public consumption and open container rules, and prescription, over-the-counter and illegal drugs. Safe driving techniques follow in the next section.

Recall emphasis: the three blood alcohol thresholds, the thirty-day permit and the refusal revocation periods are practiced as recall items; no scenario or recognition surface is needed for this section.

corpus_stability.reason: The Hawaii Driver's Manual is a periodically reprinted reference (imprint HMG 5/2023, copyright line through 2023); the the scale of the drinking-driver problem, how alcohol acts on the body, the implied consent and administrative revocation laws, zero tolerance for drivers under twenty-one, impairment thresholds, open container rules and the effects of prescription, over-the-counter and illegal drugs rules on pages 55–56 are statutory and procedural content that changes less than once a year, so no BlockedProbe.
